summary: Comprehensive testing of High-Impact security hardening (rate limit, lockout, password strength, TOTP 2FA, recovery codes, refresh-token rotation, sessions, change-password). Backend: 13/13 pytest passed. Frontend: SecuritySettings page, 2FA enable modal with QR code, Change Password form, Active Sessions list, and Sidebar nav-security all render correctly with all expected data-testids. Login page conditionally hides 2FA inputs as expected.

minor.issue: create_refresh_token JWT payload uses second-precision `exp` and no jti/nonce. If refresh is called within the same second as the previous token issuance for the same user/session_id, the rotated token equals the old one. Test had to sleep 1.2s before refresh to observe rotation. Recommend adding a jti/nonce so every rotation produces a unique token regardless of timing.

Per-IP slowapi limit is 10/min. In smoke tests / parallel test runs, fixture-based logins can hit 429 (Rate limit exceeded) and abort flows. Tests now retry on 429 with backoff. Consider raising the limit modestly (e.g. 20/min) or excluding internal/test IPs.

backend: Login returns user payload + access_token/refresh_token httpOnly cookies (non-2FA admin)
Successful login clears prior failed attempts
POST /api/security/2fa/setup returns secret + qr_code data URL + otpauth_uri
POST /api/auth/login/2fa with valid TOTP completes login
Recovery code consumes once; second use returns 401
POST /api/security/2fa/disable: rejects wrong password (401), wrong code (401), succeeds with both
GET /api/security/sessions lists sessions with exactly one current=true
POST /api/security/sessions/revoke-others revokes other sessions; current still works; revoked refresh -> 401 on /api/auth/refresh
POST /api/security/password/change rejects weak new password (400), accepts strong, can re-login with new password
POST /api/auth/refresh rotates refresh token (after >=1s gap); old refresh -> 401
Regression: GET /api/posts feed accessible after auth changes
frontend: Login page renders with login-email-input, login-password-input, login-submit-button
After login, sidebar Security nav (data-testid=nav-security) navigates to SecuritySettings via SPA state (not URL route)
SecuritySettings page renders security-settings, enable-2fa-button, change-password-form, sessions-list, current-password-input, new-password-input, confirm-new-password-input, change-password-submit
Enable 2FA modal opens and shows QR code + 2fa-confirm-code-input + Verify & Enable button
Login page does NOT render login-2fa-input on initial state (correctly conditional)
Sidebar nav 'Security' visible alongside other nav items

action_items: Optional: Add jti/nonce to refresh-token JWT payload so rotation always yields a unique token regardless of clock-second collision.
Optional: Consider raising /api/auth/login slowapi limit from 10/min or excluding test IPs to reduce CI flakiness.

Note: SecuritySettings is rendered inside Dashboard via activeView state, not a /security route. Direct URL navigation to /security falls through to default Barter Feed view. Working as designed but could be promoted to a dedicated route if deep-linking is desired.
critical_code_review_comments: security.py: clean separation of lockout / TOTP / recovery codes / refresh-store concerns; uses bcrypt for recovery code hashing (good).
auth.py routes correctly call check_lockout BEFORE find_one/verify; record_failed_attempt called on both unknown email and bad password (consistent enumeration prevention).
Refresh rotation in routes/auth.py uses find_refresh_token (revoked:false filter) + rotate_refresh_token; revoked sessions correctly fail with 401.
_set_auth_cookies uses httpOnly + secure + samesite=none + path='/' - correct for cross-site preview deployment.
SecuritySettings.js: change-password-form has both client-side confirm match + backend zxcvbn validation. Good UX.
Minor: password length hardcoded to 8 chars in security.py; could read from env for tunability.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (all key data-testids present, modal opens, conditional rendering correct)

seed_data_creation: Test created/destroyed transient login_attempts records for TEST_lockout_user@example.com and admin email, ephemerally enabled 2FA for admin during 2FA lifecycle test then disabled. Final cleanup verified admin has two_factor_enabled=false and no totp_secret/totp_pending_secret.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Security hardening features are fully verified. Reusable pytest at /app/backend/tests/test_security_hardening.py. To run: REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=<preview-url> MONGO_URL=mongodb://localhost:27017 DB_NAME=test_database pytest tests/test_security_hardening.py -v. Note: 2FA is disabled for admin after tests complete. SecuritySettings is reached via Dashboard SPA state (sidebar nav-security click), not via /security URL.
rca of the issue: No critical bugs. Single minor finding: refresh-token JWT lacks a jti/nonce, so two refresh calls within the same second produce identical JWTs. Mitigation: include `secrets.token_urlsafe(8)` as `jti` in the refresh payload inside auth.create_refresh_token.
